_note: The DSX log corpus — `dsx.log`, the unified console primitive (the logging sibling of the error system; same fixtures-first law). Every runtime (TS kernel logs.ts, Kotlin Logs.kt, Swift Logs.swift) runs these cases through ITS statement runner + log ring; deterministic, no timers, no network. THE LAW ENCODED HERE: (1) `dsx.log(...)` is variadic and console.log-shaped: each argument formats with the HOUSE coercions — scalars via JSE string coercion (booleans '1'/'0', integral numbers without '.0', null → ''), dicts/arrays as canonical minified JSON with credential-looking keys masked to '•••' (the JSERedact contract, identical on all three) — joined by single spaces. Multi-key containers are NOT pinned (Swift's JSON writer does not order keys); corpus containers stay single-key. (2) Every dsx.log records ONE structured entry { scheme, level:'log', message } in the LOG RING (cap 500, oldest evicted, always on) and mirrors one line to the platform console (Xcode / logcat / browser — DEBUG-gated where the platform gates kernel logging; the armed diagnostics drawer sees it either way). It NEVER unwinds control flow and never throws. (3) Attribution: a markup emission records the surface's owning package scheme, 'app' when unscoped; the module-handle form (`dsx.log` on a native module's own dsx) records that module's scheme; the `console.*` builtin feeds the same ring as scheme 'console' with its own level. (4) The reserved `dsx` scheme answers the `dsx.log` verb on the bus (dispatch scheme 'dsx', action 'log' — the page's `dsx.log(...)` in DSXWebView rides exactly this): args { message, scheme? } record { scheme: <scheme arg, default 'page'>, level:'log' } and resolve null; `dsx` remains refused to modules and `dsx.has('dsx')` stays false. Case ops: steps[] of jse (markup body; scheme = surface owner, default 'app') / log { scheme, args[] } (the module-handle form) / logRepeat { scheme, count, prefix } / call { scheme, action, args, mode } — expects are SUBSET-matched: logs[] = exactly the entries appended by this case in order, logCount = absolute retained total (cap case), logsTail = the newest entries, callErrors[] = codes the driven calls received, jseStore{} = store reads after a jse step.
